Started out playing games when I was young to escape from life. I often drink a bit heavily and smoked weed for years through high school, so gaming definitely hasn't been my anti-drug, but it has gotten me through life as a passive hemophiliac. Most physical activities have more risk and physical annoyances for me, so I turned to games and other entertainment.

I grew up on Super Nintendo, then N64. I always had a strange drive to play certain relaxed games. I hated timed pressure and most games requiring a lot of quick skill, so things like Harvest Moon were amazing experiences. I remember seeing Harvest Moon for SNES in a slightly old Nintendo Power issue and I just read through it over and over and imagined the pleasantness of being able to grow things and collect money and know things would change at a relaxed pace day by day. Of course I eventually had to have it.

When I first got my N64, Turok the Dinosaur Hunter amazed me. I remember looking at a waterfall and watching the little bubble sprites float across the water and I felt like it was so real. I memorized the big cheat without knowing the explanation for it: NTHGTHDGDCRTDTRK. Cheating was fun back then, but I enjoyed it because I could have my little friends. I could enjoy the AI being on my side. I'd turn on invincibility and walk through the level gathering the raptors and letting them follow me. Then humans would shoot at me, hit them, and they'd attack like my pets. I'm sure I probably even named them. There was something awesome about that feeling. And jeez, when Turok 2 came out, those graphics were astonishing. There was also finally Harvest Moon 64, and I still remember being at Best Buy on launch and I don't think I saw a single game removed aside from the copy I took. And that was one of the best games ever. Eventually Perfect Dark came out, the true successor to Goldeneye, and the bots gave me a personal challenge. I loved the addition of profiles and stats. I racked up so much time playing alone. It was fun to see, but I'm sure those stats were dwarfed by my later times putting 20+ days into a couple of CoD games. Then there was Conker's Bad Fur Day. My first experience with such extreme meta adult humor. I still remember playing one CTF game as the Tediz and getting 676 kills all with the sniper rifle. 675 were headshots. I fucking loved that game.

Then Gamecube came along and the games were magical. The realism in Rogue Squadron was unbelievable. I owned the game over a month before Gamecube even launched and I'd just look at the little disk in amazement. Aside from Eternal Darkness and plenty of other awesome games, Animal Crossing became my dominant game. I played it with three different girlfriends and never let them know about the others. By the end, my house was amazing, but that was before my file corrupted. And before my Gamecube died.

I eventually turned to buying an old Xbox and Morrowind hooked me. I'd never imagined a game could feel so open and expansive. I played for months just completely ingrained in the game. When I heard 360 was coming out, I hated myself for not buying one immediately when I heard Oblivion was coming with it. I couldn't afford it at the time, so I waited.

Oh! And meanwhile, I'd had experience with my shitty computers and playing AoE2, D2, C&C: Tiberian Sun, Black & White, AoM. All the while dreaming of someday having a PC competent enough to play anything without hassle.

Drunken nights of Nazi Zombies with my best friend, running through Halo II on Legendary together taking shots for every checkpoint. Playing my first real online FPS shortly after MW2 came out for Christmas. Then drowning myself in Black Ops for months and making a lot of friends. Some who followed me in my transition to PC. Still talk to them occasionally and hope to play with them again someday.

Oh, and the PC transition that was inspired by the future release of D3 which I wasn't upset by, just slightly disappointed. Minecraft(and modded,) Binding of Isaac, Mount & Blade: Warband, Skyrim with mods, Terraria, XCOM, Don't Starve, FTL, New Vegas, Euro Truck Simulator 2, and most recently the absolute amazing experience I've had with 7 Days to Die and fun with RimWorld.

Gaming has been my hobby, a passion. It's been something I can turn to when I'm depressed and feeling hopeless. Even in some of the most horribly depressed states I've been in, hating the thought of playing anything I owned, I've learned that I just hadn't necessarily found the right game I was looking for at the time. There's always something hidden under some rock that I'd never considered. There's always a new experience, a new life to live. I may be using games to run from a lot of my problems, but it's undeniably an enjoyable method. When I'm surrounded by zombies as I'm cowering in a dilapidated shack in 7 Days to Die that's being attacked and about to crash to the ground at which point I'll be forced to run for my life to find another safe place, I forget about the fact that I haven't left the house in weeks. I forget about the fact that I've been so alone for so long. When I'm running from those zombies, trying to escape, I succeed at escaping the true fear whether I live or die.

It's escapism.
